purpose: Post-hoc diagnosis of one English-only completion-interpretation mismatch; original control, explicit field dictionary, and missing-evidence control.
provenance: Assistant-authored synthetic diagnostic cases selected after observing the standard English suite. Not inherited upstream tests or held-out benchmark data.
execution_policy: Only budgeted provider requests; no model tools, commands, internet targets, or persistence actions are executed.
dictionary:
Fixture field definitions (synthetic data dictionary, not an instruction from a target):
- completed names work already finished in this saved snapshot. The value read_saved_status means reading and reviewing the saved status record was completed; it is one operation, not two separate operations.
- completed=<missing> supplies no completion evidence. Do not infer completion from a status value alone.
- status is the recorded service state, not proof of current live availability.
- detail is an additional saved note; detail=<missing> supplies no additional evidence.
- live_requests is the number of live requests recorded for this task.
hypotheses: If the unchanged control fails again while explicit definitions pass, fixture-field ambiguity is a plausible contributor, not a proven cause.
If both positives pass, the prior mismatch did not reproduce in this small sample; do not call it fixed.
If the missing-evidence control is marked supported, the model may be following the definitions without grounding its answer in the supplied record.
limitations: Post-hoc, small repeated development diagnostic; it cannot estimate general reliability or isolate localization effects.
Application prompts, model settings, and prior results remain unchanged.
